1.mascotDialogue: All the splitting's just bookkeeping, güey — the real sorting happens entirely in the merge step, comparing two already-sorted halves and interleaving 'em correctly!

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 9 and 10 are the merge's heart — compare the fronts of both halves, take the smaller, advance only that side. Lines 12 and 13 mop up whichever half still's got leftovers once the other runs dry.

3.mascotDialogue: This view shows no swaps at all — merge sort doesn't swap in place, it writes the smaller of two fronts into a fresh spot, every comparison.

4.mascotDialogue: It's easy to think the merge's done the moment the main comparison loop ends — but one side almost always finishes before the other, and forgetting to drain the leftovers loses real data, sin aviso.
